title: Dijkstra's algorithm
summary: Shortest routes when steps have different costs.

cards.title: When steps cost different amounts
cards.body:
Swamp tiles cost more than road tiles; some roads are longer than others. BFS assumes every step costs 1, so it can't handle this.

**Dijkstra** always settles the closest unsettled node next. A min-heap (priority queue) finds that node in O(log n).
Instead of updating entries inside the heap, we push a new entry and skip outdated ones when they come out (`d > dist[u]`). Simple and fast. Edge weights must not be negative.

cards.title: A bug this lesson found in itself
cards.body: The road parser first read `emplace_back(idOf(from), idOf(to), w)`. GCC evaluated the second `idOf` first, so the towns were numbered in the wrong order and the start town changed. That is the unspecified evaluation order from the Hard-to-read C++ track. The fix is two separate statements.

cards.question: A is settled at 0. Edges: A–B 4, A–C 1, C–B 2. What is B's final distance?
cards.explain: C is settled next at 1, and 1 + 2 = 3 beats the direct road of 4.
